high.title: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung Directs Accelerated Public Investment Disbursement, Flexible Credit Management
high.summary: The government session focused on economic-social conditions for April and Q1 2026, with Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan reporting CPI inflation accelerated to 5.46% YoY in April from 4.65% in March. The increase was driven by fuel price impacts creating chain effects on transportation, dining, and construction materials. Despite government measures reducing fuel taxes to 0% and achieving 3-20.5% price cuts through 8 adjustments, global oil prices averaging over $110/barrel kept domestic fuel costs elevated. This inflation acceleration is critical for monetary policy decisions and VND stability. The Prime Minister's directive for flexible credit management suggests potential policy adjustments ahead, while accelerated public investment disbursement could boost economic growth but also add inflationary pressure. FX traders should monitor SBV's response to these conflicting pressures.

high.title: Banks Suffer From Rising Lending Rates Creating Corporate 'Suffocation'
high.summary: Corporate lending rates have surged dramatically from 6-7% annually to nearly 9% at many banks, creating severe pressure on businesses dependent on bank financing. This represents a critical tightening in credit conditions that signals potential monetary policy transmission effects. Companies like AK FOOD report having to halt green energy investment projects due to prohibitive borrowing costs, while manufacturers face a "work more, lose more" paradox as financing costs outpace operational returns. The sharp rate increases suggest banks are either responding to SBV policy tightening or managing liquidity pressures independently. This credit tightening could slow economic growth and reduce loan demand, potentially affecting bank profitability and the broader VND/USD dynamics as foreign investors reassess Vietnam's growth prospects.

high.title: Vietcombank's Latest Interest Rates for May 2026: Which Term Offers Highest Returns?
high.summary: Vietcombank has adjusted deposit rates lower in May 2026, with the highest rate now at 6.0% annually, down from earlier April levels. Short-term deposits (1-2 months) remain at 2.1%, 3-month at 2.4%, and 6-9 month terms at 3.5%. The 12-month rate holds at 5.9%, while longer-term deposits (24 months) are at 6.0%. This rate reduction by Vietnam's largest state-owned bank signals potential easing in funding pressure and could indicate SBV policy normalization. Lower deposit rates typically strengthen bank margins but may also reflect reduced competition for deposits or policy guidance from regulators. Bond investors should note this could pressure government bond yields lower as investors seek yield alternatives, while the VND could face pressure if deposit rate cuts discourage foreign currency inflows.

medium.title: Securities Enter Month with High Probability of Index Gains, Which Stock Groups Have Money-Attracting Opportunities?
medium.summary: Analysts note that historically, when VN-Index gains over 5% in April, the probability of continued gains in May exceeds 50%. With positive momentum from global equity flows and improved market sentiment, experts suggest May could see continued market strength despite traditional "Sell in May" concerns.

medium.title: 10 Securities Companies Report Q1 Profits "Multiplied by Times", Some with Nearly 2,000% Surge
medium.summary: Ten securities firms reported massive profit increases in Q1 2026, with Tien Phong Securities (ORS) leading at 1,961% growth to 42 billion VND. The strong performance reflects improved market conditions and better cost control across the securities sector, signaling recovery in capital market activities.

medium.title: Banks with Strongest Profit Growth in Q1 2026
medium.summary: Banking sector Q1 2026 profits reached over 94,000 billion VND (+14% YoY) across 27 listed banks. Top performers included VPBank (+58%), VietinBank (+63%), BVBank (+170%), PGBank (+187%), and ABBank (+269%), indicating strong credit growth and improved operational efficiency.

medium.title: Many People Still Mispronounce BIDV Bank Name: Not "B-I-D-V" Anymore, Changed Since March
medium.summary: BIDV officially changed its brand pronunciation from "B-I-D-V" to "Bi-Di-Vi" in March 2026 to create consistency in communication and branding. The change aims to strengthen brand identity while maintaining the same written form of the bank's name.

medium.title: World's Largest Gold Fund Sold 35 Tons of Gold in Just 4 Months of Year
medium.summary: SPDR Gold Trust reduced holdings to under 1,036 tons by end-April 2026, selling 35 tons net in the first four months. The selloff reflects high interest rate environment reducing gold's attractiveness versus yield-bearing assets, with Fed holding rates at 3.5-3.75%.

medium.title: VN-Index Rises but Accounts Still Lose, What Should Investors Do?
medium.summary: VN-Index closed April at 1,854 points (+180 points monthly) but many individual investors' portfolios remain negative due to narrow market leadership concentrated in large-cap stocks. This "green shell, red core" phenomenon reflects strong market divergence where index gains don't translate to broad-based portfolio performance.

medium.title: Experts Name Two Important "Support Points" for Stock Market
medium.summary: Analysts warn of potential VN-Index correction in May as short-term catalysts from AGM season and Q1 earnings are largely priced in. The narrow market leadership creating index gains without broad participation increases vulnerability to profit-taking pressure.

medium.title: "Sell in May" Effect Really Scary for Vietnam Securities?
medium.summary: Historical data shows "Sell in May" effect is not pronounced in Vietnam's stock market. Over 25 years, VN-Index gained in May 12 times (~50% probability), but in the last 10 years, the probability increased to 70%, suggesting the effect has weakened particularly since COVID-19.
